assessment.reason: The security impact depends on the implementation of _withdraw, including whether it burns supply and transfers the correct underlying amount, as well as the arithmetic behavior of sub and the related withdrawal overload.

The function performs an external underlying-token transfer in _withdraw before updating underlyingBalance, which may permit reentrancy or create accounting inconsistencies. Assessing exploitability requires the deposit/accounting logic, constructor configuration, and token transfer behavior.

assessment.explanation: The function performs an external call to the underlying token before completing its accounting update. Because the underlying token is an arbitrary IERC20 address, a callback-capable or malicious token can reenter the wrapper while underlyingBalance still reflects the pre-withdrawal amount. Reentering deposit(address) after sending underlying tokens to the wrapper can cause incorrect net-deposit calculation and leave accounting inconsistent, enabling excess wrapped-token issuance or withdrawal. No reentrancy protection is present.

findings.vulnerability_type: Reentrancy causing stale accounting and excess token issuance
findings.explanation: _withdraw decreases totalSupply, then calls IERC20(underlying).transfer(dst, transferAmt), and only afterward subtracts transferAmt from underlyingBalance. A callback during that transfer can invoke deposit(address), which calculates the deposit amount from the stale underlyingBalance. This can mint an incorrect amount of wrapped tokens and leave underlyingBalance inconsistent with the actual underlying balance.
